MATTHEVV.|63 HOLY weeke.}}</noinclude>there is no resurrection: and asked him, {{verse|chapter=22|verse=24}}† saying, Maister, Moyses said, ''If a man die not hauing a childe, that his brother marie his wife, and raise vp seede to his brother''.{{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Deu. 25, 5.''}} {{verse|chapter=22|verse=25}}† And there vvere vvith vs seuen brethren: and the first hauing maried a wife, died: and not hauing issue, left his vvife to his brother. {{verse|chapter=22|verse=26}}† In like maner the second and the third euen to the seuenth. {{verse|chapter=22|verse=27}}† And last of al the vvoman died also. {{verse|chapter=22|verse=28}}† In the resurrection therfore vvhose vvife of the seuen shal she be? for they al had her. {{verse|chapter=22|verse=29}}† And IESVS answering, said to them, You do erre, not knowing the Scriptures, nor the povver of God. {{verse|chapter=22|verse=30}}† For in the resurrection neither shal they marie nor be maried: but are ‖ as the Angels of God in heauen. {{verse|chapter=22|verse=31}}† And concerning the resurrection of the dead, haue you not read that vvich vvas spoken of God saying to you, {{verse|chapter=22|verse=32}}† ''I am the God of Abraham, and the God of Isaac, and the God of Iacob''? He is not God ‖ of the dead, but of the liuing.{{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Exo. 3, 6.''}} {{verse|chapter=22|verse=33}}† And the multitudes hearing it, marueled at his doctrine.

{{verse|chapter=22|verse=34}}† {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Mar. 12, 28.''}}* {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=The Gospel vpō the 17 Sunday after Pentecost.}}But the Pharisees hearing that he had put the Sadducees to silence, came together: {{verse|chapter=22|verse=35}}† and one of them a doctor of law asked of him, tempting him, {{verse|chapter=22|verse=36}}† Maister, vvhich is the great commaundement in the lavv? {{verse|chapter=22|verse=37}}† IESVS said to him, ''Thou shalt loue the lord thy God from thy whole hart, and with thy whole soul, and with thy whole minde''.{{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Deut. 6, 5.''}} {{verse|chapter=22|verse=38}}† This is the greatest and the first commaundement. {{verse|chapter=22|verse=39}}† And the second is like to this, ''Thou shalt loue thy neighbour as thyself''.{{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Leu. 19, 18.''}} {{verse|chapter=22|verse=40}}† ‖ On these tvvo commaundements dependeth the vvhole Lavv and the Prophets.

{{verse|chapter=22|verse=41}}† And {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Mr. 12, 35. Lu. 20, 41.''}}* the Pharisees being assembled, IESVS asked them {{verse|chapter=22|verse=42}}† saying, What is your opinion of Christ? Whose sonne is he? They say to him, Dauids. {{verse|chapter=22|verse=43}}† He saith to them, Hovv then doth Dauid in spirit cal him Lord, saying, {{verse|chapter=22|verse=44}}† ''The Lord said to my Lord, sitte on my right hand, vntil I put thine enemies the foote stole of thy feete''?{{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Ps. 109. 1.''}} {{verse|chapter=22|verse=45}}† If Dauid therfore call him Lord, how is he his sonne? {{verse|chapter=22|verse=46}}† And no man could ansvver him a vvord: neither durst any man from that day aske him any more.⊣

{{c|{{larger|A N N O T A T I O N S}}}}
{{c|{{sc|Chap. XXII.}}}}

''2. Mariage.''] Then did God the Father make this mariage, when by the mysterie of the Incarnation he ioyned to his sonne our Lord, the holy Church for his spouse. ''Greg. hom.38''.

''3. Seruants.''] These first seruants here sent to inuite, were the Prophets: the second, were the Apostles: and al that afterward conuerted countries, or that haue and doe reconcile men to the Church.

''5. One to his farme.''] {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=Worldly excuses against reconciliation.}}Such as refuse to be reconciled to Christes Church, alleage often vaine impediments and worldly excuses, which at the day of iudgement wil not serue them.<noinclude>{{rh|||''11. A}}</noinclude>
